rules.description: All highlights removed
rules.notes: FIXED FOR REAL (2026-08-07, Round 64, item 3) -- Round 63's 'known limitation' was correctly diagnosed for the TEXT path (pypdf's plain-text extraction really does discard all color/highlight formatting) but stopped short of checking the PDF's own underlying structure, which still carries this information. Real investigation this round, against self-built synthetic ground-truth PDFs (a real highlight, a plain negative control, and a flattened-highlight-as-colored-fill case), confirmed PyMuPDF (fitz, already a pipeline dependency via render.py) can read it directly, via TWO real methods: (1) PRIMARY -- `page.annots()` filtered for `annot.type[1] == 'Highlight'` finds a real Highlight-type PDF annotation (what Word's/Adobe's highlight tools produce, same object type PyMuPDF's own `add_highlight_annot()` creates) -- confirmed live: correctly detects the synthetic real highlight, correctly finds nothing in the negative control or the flattened-fill case. (2) FALLBACK -- some export paths flatten a highlight into a colored rectangle drawn behind the text instead of a true annotation; `page.get_drawings()` filtered to a standard highlighter color (yellow/green/pink/cyan) with real text-word overlap (via `page.get_text('words')`) catches that case too -- confirmed live: correctly detects the synthetic flattened fill, which method (1) correctly cannot see (there's genuinely no annotation object there). Either method finding anything is a fail. See pipeline/fields.py::_check_TEMP03 for the implementation and the full real investigation writeup. Needs fields['pdf_path'] (the real file), not fields['full_text'].

rules.description: All correspondence with BCBA removed

The prior notes only ever described two shapes (email headers; free-form pasted chat) and never mentioned this third one, which is a well-evidenced, plausible mechanism for the narrowing even without a preserved run log to prove it conclusively (this directory has no git history of its own). See pipeline/fields.py::_check_TEMP04 and _find_embedded_reviewer_comments for the real detector: catches email-header lines AND embedded reviewer questions (distinguished from genuine clinical quoted-prompt examples like '"What is this?"' by checking whether the '?' is immediately followed by a closing quote mark) plus a small set of imperative phrasings ('please reword/clarify/specify/update/add', explicitly excluding 'please note' -- confirmed identical boilerplate template language in both real documents' Transition Plan section). Verified live: Reeda has 8 confirmed embedded reviewer comments (e.g. 'Is the Vineland for this auth?...'; 'This date is in the future, please update to correct date.'); Charny has 8 (e.g. 'Why are hours remaining the same?'; 'Please specify the DRA'). Both correctly fail now.

rules.description: Increase in hours -> rationale in place
rules.notes: Converted from judgment to deterministic (2026-07-28 round, item 2; extended the same day, follow-up round): this rule's own prior notes already said 'Presence = DET, adequacy of rationale = judgment' -- this builds the presence half in full, as TWO independent sub-checks (same 'both must hold' shape as QA-PAR-01), see pipeline/fields.py::_check_HRS06. (a) Compares each CPT code's current requested hours against that code's previous-authorization hours; where hours increased, checks for substantial (non-boilerplate) rationale text -- a presence check, not a quality judgment (QA-HRS-07 already owns rationale-quality judgment for the case where presence is confirmed). (b) Scans the Hours Requesting section for an embedded, unresolved reviewer annotation questioning an hours line item -- the same shape as QA-TRANS-01's reviewer-annotation pattern, folded into this rule rather than a new rule_id since both sub-checks are 'does this hours line item have the justification it needs' over the same section. Confirmed on both real documents, in two different structural slots: Charny -- a full question in the rationale slot itself ('Why are hours remaining the same? This rationale needs to be really strong, given the client's age... I would add a plan for titration.'); Reeda -- two short interjections in the gap before the code label ('Verifying' before 97153; 'Change if increasing' before 97155), both on codes whose hours are flat vs. the previous authorization. Verified live: both documents now correctly come back fail (sub-check (b) firing on both; sub-check (a) independently confirmed correct too -- Reeda's real 97151-Assessment increase has rationale present, Charny has no real increase anywhere). This resolves the originally-flagged miss on both documents.

rules.description: Increase in hours -> compared against previous mastery criteria
rules.notes: Previously described as needing 'stored previous-TP data' as if that meant backend-only storage this POC doesn't have. Confirmed against real documents (CS TP.pdf, Reeda Bint Shaheen's TP): the previous authorization's approved hours per CPT code ARE printed directly on the same TP's own page, under 'Hours Approved Previous Authorization:' (e.g. '97153-Direct Care by Behavior Technician 25 hours per week') -- no backend/prior-TP storage needed to read them. Compare each code's current requested hours (from the Hours Requesting section) against that same code's previous-authorization hours in this block; if a code's hours increased, check whether the accompanying clinical-rationale narrative for that code substantively addresses the increase. The data-presence half of this is a plain read; judging whether the rationale text is adequate is the genuinely judgment-based half this rule keeps.

rules.description: POS correct (home/office/school/community only)
rules.notes: Enum validation — valid values are exactly: home, office, school, community. Reclassified from deterministic to judgment (2026-07): three rounds of point-fixes each closed one specific false-match pattern (mid-word regex matches, then a blank field bleeding into the next label, then a still-unresolved case) without addressing the underlying issue — this field's real-world layout/labeling in the source PDF is too inconsistent for a fixed extraction pattern to hold up. Read the POS/place-of-service field directly from the document text and images and judge whether its value is one of the four valid options above; do not guess if the field itself is ambiguous or missing. WHICH POS SOURCE, EXPLICIT (2026-08-07, Round 64, item 2 -- confirmed real divergence: this rule and QA-GIP-09, judged in the exact same run against the exact same document, disagreed about whether Community was an authorized POS, because nothing told either rule which of TWO different 'POS' fields a real TP contains to read. A TP's School/ABA Schedule grid has its OWN 'POS' row -- that's only the SPECIFIC location(s) actually scheduled that particular week (e.g. Home on weekdays), which can be a narrower subset of what's authorized. The Hours Requesting section separately states each CPT code's AUTHORIZED place(s) of service (e.g. '97153-Direct Care ... Home, Office, and/or Community') -- this is the broader, authorizing statement, and is the correct source for THIS rule and for QA-GIP-09/QA-GIP-08. Read POS from the Hours Requesting section's stated authorized list, not the schedule grid's per-day POS row -- the schedule grid answers a different question (where sessions are actually happening this week), not this rule's question (what POS is this TP authorized for).

rules.description: At least 2 each of social/communication/behavior, narrative format
rules.notes: There is no separate DET count check for this rule -- the LLM alone must both classify AND count. Concretely: for each of the 3 buckets (Social, Communication, Behavior) find the 'Problem Area:' entries listed under that bucket's heading, and for each one check whether it has an actual 'As evidenced by:' narrative statement attached (a specific behavioral description, not a blank). An entry whose 'As evidenced by:' is missing, blank, or literally 'n/a' does NOT count toward the 2-per-bucket minimum -- it is an unevidenced problem area, not a documented one. Fail if any of the 3 buckets has fewer than 2 entries with real evidenced narrative. (Confirmed failure mode: a Behavior bucket with 4 listed 'Problem Area:' items but one item's 'As evidenced by:' is 'n/a' -- that item must be excluded from the count, and if excluding it drops any bucket below 2, this is a fail even though the bucket looked fully populated at a glance.)

rules.description: 'As evidenced by' section matches goals listed
rules.notes: Semantic alignment check -- HYBRID (2026-08-07, Round 63, item 5): confirmed real bug -- this rule passed even though one 'As evidenced by:' entry was actually a leftover embedded reviewer comment, not real clinical content, because nothing cross-checked evidence text against this pipeline's own reviewer-comment detector (QA-TEMP-04's _find_embedded_reviewer_comments). Now a deterministic pre-check: if any 'As evidenced by:' entry IS (or contains) a detected embedded reviewer comment, that alone is an unambiguous fail -- no judgment needed for that half. The genuine semantic question this rule is actually about (does the evidence align with/support the goals listed) still requires judgment and is NOT attempted deterministically -- when no reviewer-comment violation is found, this returns not_checkable, which escalates to the judgment layer for the real alignment check, unchanged. See pipeline/fields.py::_check_PROB02.

rules.description: TP includes both old and new testing tool
rules.notes: Converted from judgment to deterministic (2026-07-28 round, item 4): diagnosed as a real, previously-unfixed bug -- see pipeline/fields.py::_check_ACF07 for the full real-evidence diagnosis on both documents (Charny: entire Assessment of Current Functioning section blank, with an explicit reviewer annotation asking for it to be filled in; Reeda: ABLLS-R dated, but Vineland-3 data present with no administration date and its own embedded reviewer question asking exactly that -- 'Is the Vineland for this auth? What was the date of administration...'). The real check is: every named testing tool must have a confirmed Assessment Date tying it to a specific authorization period, or the section must not be entirely blank. Both are checkable from the TP's own text. Verified live: both real documents correctly come back fail. CLARIFIED (2026-08-06, Round 63, item 4 -- confirmed by Ms. Yachnes's own ground-truth read): 'old and new testing tool' does NOT require two DIFFERENT instruments. It is equally satisfied by the SAME tool administered twice on two different dates (an old score and a new score from one instrument) -- that is a completely normal, common re-administration pattern, not a gap. Two different tools, each dated once, still also satisfies it. What actually fails this rule is: the section is blank, a named tool has no confirmed administration date, or exactly one tool is named with only one confirmed date (in that last case: 'uncertain', not a guessed pass or fail -- a second administration may simply not be documented yet, not confirmed absent).

rules.description: Completed with clear and detailed rationale
rules.notes: Concrete rubric added (2026-07-28 follow-up round, item 3 -- 'Quick' bucket): a passing Clinical Interpretation/rationale must (1) name the client's specific presenting concerns or assessment findings (not generic boilerplate that could apply to any patient), and (2) explicitly connect those findings to the specific interventions/goals chosen. PASS example: 'Given Reeda's significant delays in functional communication and elopement-related safety concerns identified during the ABLLS-R and Vineland assessments, intensive ABA services targeting mand training and safety awareness are clinically indicated.' FAIL example: 'The client requires ABA services to address her needs and improve her skills.' -- generic, names no specific finding or client detail, could be copy-pasted into any TP. Still expect a meaningful 'Uncertain' rate on genuinely borderline cases between these two poles -- this rubric narrows the range, it doesn't eliminate judgment entirely.

rules.description: Age-appropriate mastery criteria for behavior targets
rules.notes: This rule has no concrete failure example on record yet (unlike GIP-10/GIP-16/PAR-01) -- treat the criteria below as the working standard, not a confirmed-bug fix. Check the behavior target's stated Mastery Criteria (not just the goal wording) against the client's age and the behavior's own severity/safety profile: (a) for a safety-relevant behavior (elopement, aggression, self-injury), a strict zero-occurrence criterion is normal and NOT itself a fail; (b) flag only when the criterion is developmentally mismatched in a way you can point to in the text -- e.g. a criterion phrased for a skill far beyond the client's documented developmental/cognitive level, a criterion with no duration/session-count qualifier at all (just a bare percentage with no consistency window), or a criterion that ignores a stated generalization requirement (e.g. across settings/people) that the rest of the plan otherwise expects. Do not fail solely because a criterion sounds strict for a young child -- strictness alone is not the defect; an unexplained mismatch between the criterion's demand and the client's documented profile is.

rules.description: All goals match the POS
rules.notes: Concrete example added (2026-07-28 follow-up round, item 3 -- 'Quick' bucket; NOT a DET-conversion candidate -- see QA-SCH-08's own notes for why this field's real-world layout is too inconsistent for a fixed extraction pattern, confirmed against real documents in an earlier round). CORRECTED (2026-08-07, Round 63, item 8 -- confirmed real bug: this rule was passing goals that state no setting information at all, on the theory that 'no goal names a CONFLICTING setting' = compliant. That's wrong: goals saying NOTHING about setting is an inability to confirm compliance, not evidence of it, and must not default to pass.) Three distinct outcomes, not two: (1) PASS -- at least one goal's own narrative affirmatively states a setting, and every goal that states one is consistent with the declared Place of Service (e.g. POS is Office/Home/Telehealth/Community, and a goal reading 'client will complete the task across settings including office and home' names only setting(s) POS covers). (2) FAIL -- ANY goal's narrative names a setting the declared POS does NOT cover (e.g. POS is 'Office' only, but a goal reads 'client will complete the task in the community setting' or 'at home without BT present'). (3) NOT_CHECKABLE -- no goal anywhere in the document states any setting/POS information at all; this is a genuine inability to confirm the goals match the POS, not a clean pass by default. Do not collapse (3) into (1) just because there's no explicit conflict -- absence of a stated conflict is not the same as confirmed compliance. WHICH POS SOURCE, EXPLICIT (2026-08-07, Round 64, item 2 -- same fix applied to QA-GIP-09/QA-SCH-08 after a confirmed real divergence between those two rules over this exact ambiguity): read the 'declared Place of Service' above from the Hours Requesting section's stated authorized place(s) of service per CPT code, NOT the School/ABA Schedule grid's per-day POS row -- the schedule grid shows only where sessions are actually scheduled this particular week, a real, potentially narrower subset of what's authorized, and is the wrong source for this rule's own POS comparison.

FAIL example: POS includes Community, but no goal anywhere in the document mentions community/generalization-across-settings at all. If POS doesn't include Community, not_applicable. Same document, same underlying fact, contradictory conclusions.): read Place of Service from the SAME source as QA-SCH-08 -- the Hours Requesting section's stated authorized place(s) of service per CPT code (e.g. '97153-Direct Care ... Home, Office, and/or Community'), NOT the School/ABA Schedule grid's per-day POS row. The schedule grid only shows which specific location(s) sessions are actually happening at THIS week -- a real, potentially narrower subset of what's authorized -- and is the wrong source for 'does POS include Community' questions in this rule or QA-SCH-08/QA-GIP-08.

rules.description: Sampling method consistent across baseline/current/sampling/mastery
rules.notes: Converted from judgment to deterministic (2026-07-28 round, item 1): this is a uniqueness/consistency check over a code-extractable list of per-goal field values, not a holistic reasoning task -- see pipeline/fields.py::_check_GIP10 for the implementation and its full rationale. Splits the document on every 'Target Goal:' marker (goals can span a page boundary), then for each goal block with a 'Sampling Method:' field checks: (a) the value matches a known method name (catches both a broken merge-field artifact like literal 'Page' and spelling/wording variants like 'Precent correct' or 'percentage correct'); (b) Baseline and Mastery Criteria are non-blank (catches a goal with a valid Sampling Method but a missing companion field). Verified live against both Reeda's and Charny's real documents against the already-known outliers: Reeda -- page 32 'Precent correct' (typo), page 37 'Page' (broken merge field), page 52 'percentage correct' (wording variant); Charny -- page 27, a Frequency-sampled goal with a blank Mastery Criteria. All four were correctly caught; no false positives on either document's other 30+ goals.

rules.description: Goals in behavioral context (SD, setting, expected response)
rules.notes: No confirmed failure example on record yet -- treat as the working standard, not a confirmed-bug fix. A passing goal's Target Goal text must contain, explicitly or unambiguously implied, all 3 elements: (1) an SD/antecedent condition -- what cues or triggers the behavior (e.g. 'when told no', 'when a demand is given', 'when BT is distracted'); (2) a setting/context if the goal is context-dependent (e.g. 'in a conversation', 'during a task'); (3) an expected response stated as an observable action, not a vague internal state (e.g. 'will mand by calling BT's name' is fine; 'will feel less anxious' is not, because there's no observable response). Fail when the antecedent condition is entirely missing (the goal reads as a bare behavior with no stated trigger) or when the expected response is an internal/emotional state with no observable action attached -- not merely because the goal is short.

FAIL example: a goal reading only 'client will communicate needs appropriately' with no operant term (mand/tact/echoic/intraverbal/etc.) named anywhere, and no atypical-but-recognizable phrasing for one either (e.g. 'will request' counts as mand-shaped even without the word 'mand' itself -- only fail when the goal names no functional communication category at all).

rules.description: Mastery criteria age/ASD-appropriate; no 0%, use 'fewer than one instance'
rules.notes: Converted from judgment to deterministic (2026-07-28 round, item 1 backlog): the zero/near-zero-endpoint ban is a per-goal pattern check over an extractable field (Mastery Criteria), same shape as GIP-10 -- see pipeline/fields.py::_check_GIP16, which shares GIP-10's _goal_block_starts helper. Scope note: this DET check covers ONLY the zero-value-ban half of the rule's description ('no 0%, use fewer than one instance'); the broader 'age/ASD-appropriate' framing in the description is not separately implemented here since no distinct check for it was ever built or described beyond the zero-ban itself -- if a genuinely separate age-appropriateness judgment is intended beyond the zero-ban, that would need its own rule/check. This ban applies to BOTH percentage-based AND frequency-based mastery criteria - do not treat frequency/count goals as exempt just because they don't use a percent sign. A mastery criterion is a violation if it states a zero or near-zero endpoint in ANY of these forms: '0%', '0 occurrences', '0x', 'near 0 levels', 'near 0', or equivalent zero-value phrasing - regardless of Sampling Method (Percent Correct or Frequency). Any of these must instead read 'fewer than one instance' (or an equivalent minimum-occurrence phrasing). Verified live: Reeda has exactly 2 confirmed violations (page 26 Tantrum, page 27 Elopement, both in 'Target Name:' Behavior Reduction Goal blocks -- not 'Target Goal:' ones, which is why the shared block-splitter covers both marker forms). Charny has zero violations (one goal reads '0-2 occurrences over three consecutive days', correctly NOT flagged since it's a range, not a zero endpoint). EXPLICIT DIVISION OF LABOR WITH QA-GIP-10 (2026-08-07, Round 63, item 7): a BLANK Mastery Criteria is a real problem, but this rule's own zero/near-zero pattern never matches an empty string, so on its own this would silently pass a blank field -- QA-GIP-10 already flags a blank Mastery Criteria, but ONLY for a goal block that also has a Sampling Method field (it skips any block without one). This rule now flags the one remaining gap -- a blank Mastery Criteria in a block with NO Sampling Method field either -- and deliberately does NOT also flag the Sampling-Method-present case, to avoid two rules reporting the same blank-field violation as if it were two separate problems. If both this rule and QA-GIP-10 pass on the same document, that means every Mastery Criteria field found is confirmed non-blank; a not_checkable from either is not itself evidence of a blank field.

rules.description: Goals observable/measurable with SD, deficit, expectation
rules.notes: Same family as GIP-11 -- same caution: no confirmed failure example on record yet, working standard only. A passing goal must contain: (1) an SD/antecedent condition (what prompts the target); (2) a deficit statement -- what the client currently cannot do or does incorrectly, stated concretely enough that progress against it is measurable; (3) an expectation stated as an observable, countable action (percent correct, count, duration -- not a vague internal-state description). Fail when the goal is observable/measurable in form (has a Mastery Criteria percentage) but the Target Goal text itself never states what deficit is being remediated, or when the antecedent condition is missing entirely -- a goal can have a perfectly quantitative Mastery Criteria and still fail this rule if the goal statement itself doesn't establish what's being measured and why.

rules.description: 3+ parent training goals/auth period, no 'caregiver' wording (or rationale if used)
rules.notes:
Two independent criteria, both must hold -- confirmed via real evidence on two documents that a compressed one-line description let both slip past unnoticed:
(1) At least 3 distinct parent-training goals exist for THIS authorization period. Count only goals under 'Goals in Progress' / currently active for this auth period -- do NOT count goals listed under 'Mastered Goals' toward this total, even if they use parent-training wording, since those are from a prior period. (Confirmed failure mode: a document with 4 'Mastered Goals' phrased as parent-training goals but only 1 actually current/in-progress goal -- the '3+' requirement is about the current period, and miscounting mastered history toward it produces a false pass.)
(2) No individual CURRENT goal's own Target Goal text uses 'caregiver' as its subject (e.g. 'The caregiver will...') instead of 'parent'/'parents'/'mother'/'father', unless that specific goal has its own accompanying rationale for the wording choice. IMPORTANT: this document type routinely uses 'Parent/Caregiver' as standard SECTION-HEADER and narrative terminology (e.g. 'Parent/Caregiver Involvement:', 'Parent/Caregiver Goals:', 'caregivers are coached on...') -- that widespread usage is NOT itself a violation and must not be read as making 'caregiver' wording normal everywhere in the document. The actual check is narrower: does any individual CURRENT goal's own subject specifically say 'caregiver' while its sibling current goals say 'parent(s)'/'mother'/'father'? That specific inconsistency, without a rationale for that one goal, is a fail -- even though the rest of the document uses 'caregiver' extensively elsewhere as its own header/section-naming convention.
COUNTING SCOPE (confirmed second false-pass mechanism, on a document where the mastered-goals exclusion above was already applied correctly): only count entries listed literally under a 'Parent/Caregiver Goals:' (or equivalent parent-training goal list) heading for the current period. A 'Transition Plan' / hours-titration section that discusses parent training being 'mastered and maintained' in its narrative, or that lists the PATIENT's own skill-mastery criteria in a numbered table (e.g. 'When [patient] can make 5 relevant comments...'), is not a parent-training goal and must not be counted toward the 3+ total just because it sits near parent-training language or references future parent-training phases. If, after excluding both Mastered Goals and any non-goal-list narrative/tables, fewer than 3 distinct current parent-training goals remain, this is a fail regardless of how much surrounding text discusses parent involvement generally.

KNOWN LIMITATION -- NOT FIXED (2026-08-07, Round 63): a confirmed real miss requires connecting a fact stated in a COMPLETELY DIFFERENT section (the patient's foster-care status, mentioned under Biopsychosocial Information) to whether 'caregiver' wording in THIS section's goals is actually justified (a foster family situation can be a legitimate reason 'caregiver' is the more accurate term than 'parent'). That is real cross-section reasoning -- reading one fact in one part of the document and applying it as context for a wording judgment in an entirely different part -- which this rule's text-pattern approach cannot do today. This is deliberately left unaddressed rather than patched with a special case that keys off the literal phrase 'foster care' (or any other single magic phrase): a narrow keyword special-case would look fixed for this one scenario while remaining just as blind to every other legitimate cross-section reason a document might have for using 'caregiver' (a grandparent guardian, a court-appointed guardian, a group-home placement, etc.). Closing this for real needs the judgment layer to be given BOTH sections' content together with an explicit instruction to check for a stated justification anywhere in the document, not a single keyword rule -- that is a real capability gap, not a copyediting fix, and is flagged here rather than routed around.

rules.description: Patient-specific and realistic based on goals
rules.notes: 'Matches the Learning Tree' wording ignored per Section 14. The real check here is NOT a general judgment call on goal specificity/realism (that's a fallback only) — the manual reviewer's own embedded note asks for a status sentence on every Transition Plan goal, and it isn't there. Look for a reviewer-embedded comment/highlighted annotation near the Transition Plan section requesting a status update on Transition Plan goals (the same kind of embedded PDF annotation as a severity-rating note elsewhere in this rule set). If that reviewer note is present: check every individual Transition Plan goal in the document for a short status sentence attached to it, and fail if any goal lacks one — this is a per-goal presence check, not a subjective realism judgment. If no such reviewer note is present anywhere near the Transition Plan section, fall back to the general judgment call on whether goals are patient-specific and realistic.

rules.notes: Relabeled from deterministic to judgment (2026-07-28 round): the old regex-based duplicate-bullet-marker checker (_find_repeated_bullet_markers, shared with QA-DISC-02) produced a confirmed false positive on Reeda's real TP -- it matched '3. 3.' on page 61, which is NOT a leftover copy-paste duplicate but a genuine two-column table-layout artifact: the Goal Name column's '3.' label and the Mastery Criteria column's '3.' label for the same row ended up textually adjacent because the goal's own descriptive paragraph (which normally separates them) spilled onto the next page. A text-only regex cannot distinguish 'same number labeling two different table columns for one row' from 'an actually duplicated marker' -- this is the same class of problem QA-SCH-08 was reclassified for (see pipeline/CHECKER_DESIGN.md), not a one-off regex bug worth a fourth patch.

rules.description: Patient-specific and realistic based on goals
rules.notes: Concrete example added (2026-07-28 follow-up round, item 3 -- 'Quick' bucket): restates QA-TRANS-01's own mechanism explicitly here rather than only cross-referencing it, per an earlier round's flag that a bare cross-reference risks silently going stale if TRANS-01's notes ever change. Same two-step check: (1) look for a reviewer-embedded comment/annotation near the Discharge Criteria section requesting a status update on discharge goals; if present, check every individual Discharge Criteria goal for a short status sentence, fail if any lacks one -- a per-goal presence check, not a subjective realism judgment. (2) If no such reviewer note exists near this section, fall back to the general judgment of whether the discharge criteria are patient-specific and realistic given the goals in the rest of the document (PASS example: criteria tied to this patient's actual named goals reaching mastery; FAIL example: generic boilerplate criteria that could apply to any patient, e.g. 'services will be discharged when appropriate').

rules.description: Goal dates within 30 days of authorization start date
rules.notes: Docx wording: 'Date of goals is within 30 days of start.' NOT built this round -- genuine scope ambiguity, not a missing-checker gap. Real TPs (CS TP.pdf, Reeda Bint Shaheen's TP) show 'Goals in Progress' contains a mix of goals with Date Initiated values many months old (legitimately still in progress from a prior authorization) alongside a distinct 'New Goals:' section for goals newly added this cycle.
